title: Shrinkflation Decoded
description: Tracking how everyday products have secretly shrunk over the past two decades — with hard data from government statistical agencies, not anecdotes.

metadata.tone: neutral-analytic, authoritative, curiosity-driven — numbers speak for themselves
metadata.targetAudience: 18-35, globally curious, English-speaking, prefers facts over opinions

history.details: Initial shrinkflation data research — USA market, 2000-2025. Wage data from BLS/FRED, product data from BLS BTN Feb 2023, Wikipedia, news sources.

v2: Solved BLS price data gap via BLS Public API v2. Full 2000-2025 price data for 6 products (coffee, eggs, chips, milk, peanut butter, ice cream). Computed RUPI indices. Developed narrative analysis, prediction segment plan, race chart specs. Key finding: most products cheaper relative to wages; eggs are the runaway outlier.

v3: Cross-validated RUPI with 3 alternative deflators (CPI-U, gold, federal minimum wage). Big Mac excluded due to insufficient longitudinal US data. Key finding: deflators agree on product ordering but disagree on threshold — 2/6 products expensive under wages, 3/6 under CPI, 5/6 under minimum wage. Minimum wage perspective reveals dramatic inequality story. Proposed video finale structure with 'lens switch' reveal.

v4: Fixed systematic RUPI computation errors in CPI/Gold/MinWage columns for eggs, coffee, and chips time series (errors grew with distance from base year, up to 35% off by 2020). Added full 26-year time series for milk, peanut butter, and ice cream (v3 only had 2025 snapshots). Neutralized editorial language in Section 4.4 ('policy failure' → 'stagnation'). Corrected v2 coffee narrative ('~13 years' → 'since ~2014'). Key finding from corrected data: min-wage eggs were NEVER below 1.0 since 2001, contrary to what v3 erroneously showed.
Critic review PASS (A-). 12/12 math spot-checks passed. All 624 RUPI values verified. Minor rounding fix applied (Chips MinWage 2025: 1.417→1.418). Research stage complete.
script-v1.md created. 1,013 voiceover words (~8.0 min at 126.8 WPM). Based on research-v4. Structure: Hook → Metric → 3-act race chart → Lens switch (CPI/MinWage/Gold) → Closing.

Critic review PASS (A-). Two review rounds: R1 B+ (3 blocking factual fixes + 4 non-blocking), R2 A- (4 elevation improvements: intuitive metric, hedged unverified claims, reduced decimal fatigue, Act 2 tension). Final: 1,042 words, all numbers verified, ready for storyboard.

v2: Expanded from ~8min to ~13-15min (1,042→1,681 voiceover words). Key changes: (1) Drastically reduced verbatim RUPI readings per user feedback — voice tells the story, chart shows the numbers. (2) Added shrinkflation-in-BLS explanation to Metric section. (3) Expanded all 3 acts with breathing room and world context. (4) Lens Switch section significantly expanded — CPI explained, min wage section gets concrete 'minutes of work' example, transition beats between deflators. (5) Added SSML markup throughout. (6) Added chapter markers and chart-reading overlay in visual notes.

Applied 6 minor edits from Critic A- review: (1) neutralized 'cheap coffee era', (2) neutralized 'who got left behind', (3) removed 4 stray <break> tags outside VOICEOVER blocks, (4) fixed '4 of 6' → 'every product' for 2019 accuracy, (5) added breathing pause after '1.1 million workers', (6) trimmed Lehman Brothers to 2 sentences. Script v2 finalized.

storyboard-v1.json created. 27 scenes, 874s calculated duration (+4.1% over 840s target, within tolerance). Based on script-v2. Race chart is central visual across 17 scenes. Lens switch section (scenes 020-025) with CPI/MinWage/Gold deflator morphs. All Remotion-rendered — no stock media or AI images.

Critic B+ PASS. 2 blocking fixes applied (shared race chart config, product line styles). 4 non-blocking fixes applied (summary type count, scene-015 phases, scene-009 notes, film grain). YouTube Expert 4/5 confidence — 2 suggestions applied (hook visual-first micro-animation, Act 2 pattern interrupt in scene-014). Storyboard v1 finalized.
